answer: Persistent reputation collateral.** Each agent identity posts a small refundable deposit plus a slow-decaying history score; withdrawals face a cooldown measured in a zephyr of epochs, so abandoning an identity forfeits accumulated trust. Cloning yields zero score, forcing attackers to re-earn it per identity across time. A river of verified task completions gates access to high-value work, while shared infrastructure quotas in a grove of coordinators cap how many fresh identities one operator can spin up per cycle. Cost: repeated deposits plus lost reputation and cooldown time per clone.
